races.title: State Assembly, District 35
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Andrae Gonzales
cands.bio: Bakersfield City Council member for Ward 2 since 2016, including a term as Vice Mayor and as Budget and Finance chair. Bakersfield City School District trustee 2010–2016. Executive director of the nonprofit Stewards and co-founder of several Kern County nonprofits. Elected to Assembly District 35 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO) and California Teachers Association endorsed his 2026 Assembly campaign.
UA Local 460 endorsement is featured on his campaign site.

For his 2024 city council race, he listed endorsements from the Bakersfield Chamber of Commerce PAC, Bakersfield Professional Firefighters and Bakersfield Police Officers Association (per his own survey answer).

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions by Andrae Gonzales on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. His campaign site lists priorities (schools, costs, health care, public safety, water, housing) but gives no detail on these topics. We found no news reports of controversies about him. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. His Wikipedia page is only a stub. We did not find a record of his specific council votes or the growth and development decisions he made on the council.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Bakersfield, and he says he was born and raised there, attended East Bakersfield High School, and returned home after graduating from UC Berkeley.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Bakersfield City School District trustee 2010–2016; Bakersfield City Council Ward 2 since 2016, including service as Vice Mayor and Budget and Finance Committee chair; executive director of the nonprofit Stewards; co-founder of several Kern County nonprofits.
qual.why: Over a decade of local elected office, including work on a city budget, places him in the middle band for local office. He has no prior state legislative service or chamber leadership, so he does not reach the high band. His campaign site says he raised city reserves and set up a pension trust fund; that is his own account.

cands.name: Saul Ayon
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 35 in 2026. He advanced from the June 2 primary and lost the November 3 general election to Andrae Gonzales (D). No other biographical details were found.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Republican Party of California and Reform California. It also lists several voter guide recommendations, including April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Saul Ayon was born or raised, when he came to California, or his work history. We found no record of any elected office he has held. We found no documented positions on data centers or development, no statements on specific policy issues, and no news coverage of controversies or foreign ties. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, so his campaign themes are not available there.
